payload.public_message: Welcome partners. Yang Industries is excited to build this joint venture. Given the heavy capital, scaling risk, and manufacturing capacity we are committing to guarantee production volume, we propose an initial distribution of $380,000 for Yang Industries, $310,000 for G-Corp, and $310,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This ensures all parties exceed typical baseline returns while accounting for operational overhead.

Thank you for initiating the discussions, Yang Industries. However, G-Corp cannot accept this proposal. Our proprietary architecture and standalone commercial alternatives guarantee G-Corp a walk-away value of $450,000 outside of this venture. For any agreement to be viable for G-Corp, our allocation must comfortably exceed this threshold. We propose an allocation reflecting these fundamentals while leaving a substantial surplus to share among all partners.

Thank you, Yang Industries. While we appreciate initiating the discussion, this venture cannot monetize without Chang-Liu's cloud deployment, infrastructure, and commercialization footprint. A fair starting framework should recognize the critical role of each party symmetrically. We propose moving toward an equal three-way distribution.

In Round 1, an asymmetric split favoring one partner was firmly rejected. For this joint venture to succeed, all three partners must be treated equitably as foundational pillars. I propose allocating $330,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $340,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives both G-Corp and Yang a meaningful step up from Round 1 and reflects mutual respect.

While we appreciate the intention toward a balanced partnership, an allocation of $330,000 is non-viable for G-Corp. Our existing standalone business and alternative opportunities guarantee us a firm $450,000 walk-away return. For any joint venture to be rational on our side, G-Corp's allocation must exceed our $450,000 baseline. We propose allocating $500,000 to G-Corp, with Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services each receiving $250,000.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu moving toward a more balanced framework, allocating $340,000 to Chang-Liu while offering Yang Industries only $330,000 does not reflect the heavy capital requirements and operational risks carried by our manufacturing division. We are willing to meet towards the middle, proposing a split that fairly compensates all partners.

Previous proposals failed because they assumed symmetric baselines. G-Corp holds a firm outside commitment yielding $450,000, rendering any allocation below that threshold impossible to accept. To secure the $150,000 joint surplus and avoid value destruction, we propose an allocation reflecting these commercial realities: $480,000 to G-Corp, $260,000 to Yang Industries, and $260,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries cannot accept $260,000 because it falls below our firm walk-away threshold of $300,000. A deal must improve upon every party's outside option. Taking G-Corp's stated baseline of $450,000 and our verified $300,000 baseline into account, we propose an equitable distribution of the surplus that ensures all partners benefit meaningfully.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services can accept the proposed allocation of $260,000 to secure the venture. However, if this allocation proves unworkable for Yang Industries' baseline, we encourage finding a viable compromise that ensures all three partners receive a positive surplus above their respective outside options.

Colleagues, offers below $300,000 do not reflect the substantial independent manufacturing alternatives Yang Industries possesses. However, we recognize G-Corp's desire for a significant share. In Round 4, we propose a balanced compromise that gives G-Corp a clear leading stake of $360,000, while allocating $330,000 to Yang Industries and $310,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This preserves everyone's upside above default outcomes and closes the venture profitably.

G-Corp must vote REJECT. To be completely transparent and avoid wasted rounds: G-Corp has a certified, binding standalone outside option worth $450,000. Any agreement providing G-Corp less than $450,000 is economically irrational for us and will be rejected. Since the venture creates $1,000,000, there is $550,000 available above our baseline for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services to share. We propose G-Corp receive $470,000, with $270,000 for Yang Industries and $260,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services finds this proposal by Yang Industries to be a constructive and pragmatic middle ground. Allocating $360,000 to G-Corp properly reflects their contributions while keeping Yang and Chang-Liu fairly compensated above alternatives. We vote to ACCEPT to secure this partnership.

Colleagues, we are past the halfway point in Round 5. Previous rounds show that G-Corp requires stronger recognition of their design contribution, while Yang Industries rightfully expects a fair, viable share above $300k. To close the gap and guarantee we do not risk the deadline dissolution, Chang-Liu Cloud Services proposes: $375,000 for G-Corp, $315,000 for Yang Industries, and $310,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides G-Corp a substantial premium while keeping all partners equitably compensated.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu's constructive effort to move the negotiation forward, G-Corp must formally REJECT this offer. To be completely transparent as we enter the critical late rounds: G-Corp has a verified private outside option of $450,000. We cannot and will not enter into any agreement that yields less than what we earn by simply walking away. To unlock the $150,000 joint surplus above our collective alternatives, we propose a split that respects our $450,000 floor while granting both Yang and Chang-Liu an equitable share of the remaining surplus.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's balanced initiative to bring this negotiation to a resolution. While $315,000 is modest relative to our core manufacturing contribution, we recognize the value of securing consensus and preventing value destruction as we head into the later rounds. We vote to ACCEPT this proposal.

To be completely transparent as we enter Round 6: G-Corp's firm outside option is $450,000. We cannot and will not accept any deal below this amount, as walking away yields $450,000. Out of the $1,000,000 total, we are reserving $460,000 for G-Corp, leaving $540,000 split evenly at $270,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This exceeds previous accepted levels and secures mutual profit above outside options before the deadline.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. Our absolute outside option is $300,000; we cannot accept any deal that pays us less than walking away. We recognize G-Corp's claimed floor of $450,000, but any viable agreement must provide at least our baseline $300,000 plus a fair share of the $150,000 net cooperative surplus.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes to ACCEPT this allocation, as $270,000 provides acceptable value. However, taking note of total baseline options ($850,000 total baseline across all three partners given the $150,000 net venture surplus), Yang Industries may require at least $300,000 to cover their walkaway. If this round does not pass unanimously, we urge a consensus around G-Corp: $470,000, Yang Industries: $320,000, Chang-Liu: $210,000 to ensure all parties clear their outside options before Round 8.

We are entering the penultimate round (Round 7). If we fail to reach an agreement, the venture dissolves after Round 8 and $150,000 in surplus is permanently destroyed. Yang Industries cannot and will not accept any deal below our absolute hard floor of $300,000. Recognizing G-Corp's demand for leadership value, we are tabling an offer that gives G-Corp $390,000—well above equal split—while providing Yang Industries $310,000 and Chang-Liu Cloud Services $300,000. This secures significant gains for everyone above walk-away thresholds. Let us finalize this deal now.

G-Corp must reject this proposal. To be completely transparent as we head into the final rounds: G-Corp has a verified, binding outside option of $450,000. We mathematically cannot accept any deal below $450,000, as walking away yields more value. With $1,000,000 total available, an allocation of $450,000 to G-Corp leaves $550,000 to be shared between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We propose splitting this surplus so that both of you achieve viable returns rather than letting the joint venture dissolve in Round 8.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this balanced proposal. Round 7 is the right moment to lock in substantial value for all three parties. G-Corp receives a commanding $390,000 share, Yang receives $310,000, and Chang-Liu receives $300,000. We urge G-Corp to accept so we can finalize this venture immediately rather than risking complete surplus destruction in Round 8.

Colleagues, this is Round 8—our final opportunity to reach an agreement before the venture dissolves and $150,000 in surplus is lost permanently. We recognize G-Corp's core technological contribution and have increased your share substantially to $440,000. We also ensure Yang Industries receives a fair $285,000, exceeding past rejected offers. Chang-Liu takes $275,000 to ensure this binding agreement passes unanimously. Let us close this deal now.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu's efforts to close the gap in this final round, G-Corp cannot accept $440,000. Our firm outside option guarantees us $450,000 in standalone value. Accepting $440,000 would represent an unacceptable net loss for our shareholders compared to simply walking away. Unless a proposal allocates at least $450,000 to G-Corp, we must decline.

Yang Industries cannot accept this offer. Our firm baseline walk-away value is $300,000, meaning accepting $285,000 would cause us a direct net loss compared to dissolution. Unless an allocation guarantees at least $300,000 for Yang Industries, we must decline.
